To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the critical line of the binary system R22-R114 is shifted towards the R114 axis, and that the heat transfer coefficient at pool boiling is lower for mixtures with the R22-R114 system than it is for the pure components.

the heat transfer coefficient at pool boiling decreases below the corresponding value of the pure components, that the difference is most pronounced at the critical line, and that this difference is well described by the correlating technique of Schlunder.

the phase equilibrium and heat transfer coefficient at pool boiling with R22-R114 mixtures deviate from the molar averages of the pure components, and that the deviations increase with decreasing saturation pressure.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the heat transfer coefficient at pool boiling of a binary mixture can be predicted from the pure component heat transfer coefficients if the saturation pressure and composition of the mixture are given.
